title: Confirm Discover prerequisites without promising inclusion
statement: Before any Discover work is proposed, the documented prerequisites are checked and reported as prerequisites, and no report states or implies that satisfying them causes the site to appear on the surface.
rationale: The prerequisites are the only part of this surface that is documented and observable, so a report that presents them as a route to appearing is asserting something the operator does not publish.
implementation: Report which prerequisites hold and which do not, and describe the outcome as selection by the surface. Do not attach a projected traffic figure or a timeline to the work.

verification.method: Read the generated Discover section of the report and confirm every statement is either a checked prerequisite or an explicit statement that inclusion is not controllable.

caution: The cited documentation describes what makes content eligible and states that appearing is not guaranteed. This record exists to stop eligibility being reported as inclusion, which is the most common overclaim in this area.

title: Write headlines that match what the page delivers
statement: The headline states the substance of the article rather than withholding it, and a reader who acts on the headline finds the thing it led them to expect.
rationale: A headline that withholds its own subject to create curiosity misrepresents the page, and the reader who arrives and leaves immediately was misled rather than served.
implementation: Put the specific claim in the headline and let the article expand it. Report headlines that appear to withhold their subject and leave the wording to whoever is accountable for the article.

verification.method: Compare each headline against the visible primary heading and the opening passage, reporting headlines whose subject appears in neither.

caution: The cited policy names misleading and exaggerated headlines as disallowed, which supports reporting them. Rewriting a headline is an editorial act with attribution consequences, so this record never applies a change automatically.

title: Publish a wide representative image for each article
statement: Each article carries an image at least the documented width, sized and cropped so its subject survives being displayed at a different aspect ratio, and reachable without a credential.
rationale: A narrow or logo-only image cannot be presented at the size this surface uses, and an image whose subject sits at one edge loses that subject when the surface crops it.
implementation: Store one wide original per article and derive the smaller variants from it, keeping the subject near the centre so a crop to a different ratio still contains it.

verification.method: Fetch the declared article image for each route and record its pixel width, its aspect ratio, and the status returned.

caution: Meeting the documented width makes a large presentation possible rather than certain. Which image a surface displays, and whether it displays one at all, is the surface's decision.

title: Permit large image previews where the site wants them
statement: Where large previews are intended, the robots directive permitting them is present on the article routes, and no narrower preview limit is emitted elsewhere for the same route.
rationale: The default preview limit is smaller than the presentation these routes are prepared for, so an article with a compliant image can still be shown without one because a directive restricts it.
implementation: Emit the directive on the article routes only, leaving routes whose imagery should not be enlarged at the default. Check the header and the document for a second directive that would contradict the first.

verification.method: Collect the preview directives from both the response headers and the document for each article route and report routes carrying more than one distinct limit.

caution: Permitting a larger preview grants permission and nothing more. It does not cause a large preview to be shown, and it should not be set on routes whose images the site does not want enlarged.

sources.title: Robots meta tag, data-nosnippet, and X-Robots-Tag specifications

title: Show a visible byline and publisher on editorial pages
statement: Each article names the person or desk responsible for it and the publication it belongs to, in text a reader can see, not only inside structured data.
rationale: A reader deciding whether to trust an article looks for who wrote it, and an attribution that exists only in machine-readable markup answers that question for nobody.
implementation: Render the byline near the headline and link it to a page describing that author or desk. Report articles with no attribution rather than assigning one.

verification.method: Extract visible attribution text from each article route, report routes where attribution appears only in structured data or nowhere at all, and confirm with the publisher that each named author wrote the piece attributed to them.

caution: The cited guidance asks who produced the content and why a reader should trust it, which supports visible attribution without documenting it as a requirement, so this record is tier B. Attribution is never invented, because naming the wrong person is worse than naming nobody.

title: Read Discover performance only from the platform report
statement: Any statement about how the site performs on this surface comes from the operator's own report for that property, and the absence of the report is recorded as no data rather than as no traffic.
rationale: Referral traffic from this surface is not reliably distinguishable in a site's own analytics, so a figure derived locally is a guess presented with the authority of a measurement.
implementation: Record whether the report exists for the property and quote it where it does. Where it does not, say the data is unavailable and stop, instead of substituting a referral estimate.

verification.method: Confirm every performance statement about this surface cites the operator report with the date it was read, and that no statement is derived from local referral data.

caution: The report only appears once the property has enough activity to populate it, so its absence carries no information either way. That asymmetry is why this record forbids inferring absence of traffic from absence of the report.
